stem.en:
Nilufar's family keeps three hens in a small coop behind their house. In winter the hens lay fewer eggs, so from November to February Nilufar's mother buys extra eggs at the market. In spring, when the days grow longer, the hens lay enough eggs for the whole family again.

According to the text, why does Nilufar's mother buy eggs at the market from November to February?

options.en: The family's hens lay fewer eggs in the winter months.
Eggs at the market are cheaper in the winter months.
The family sells its own eggs at the market in winter.
The hens are kept inside the house during the winter.

why.en: The text says 'In winter the hens lay fewer eggs, so' she buys extra: the hens lay fewer eggs then. Prices and selling eggs are never mentioned.
why.uz: Matnda qishda tovuqlar kamroq tuxum qilgani uchun onasi qoʻshimcha tuxum sotib olishi aytilgan. Narx yoki tuxum sotish haqida gap yoʻq.

She takes the bus that comes back at five.

When Feruza started selling her embroidered bags online, she expected most orders to come from her own city. Instead, her first fifty orders came from twelve different towns, and only six were from nearby. She now spends Monday mornings packing parcels and takes them to the post office before lunch, so that they leave with the afternoon van.

Based on the text, what is true about Feruza's first fifty orders?

Most of them came from her own city, as she had expected.
All of them were posted on the same Monday afternoon.

One spring his bicycle chain broke, and he had to walk the longer way, through the apple orchards and past the old mill. He wanted to arrive at his grandmother's in a good mood.
The highway was closed for repairs that spring.
His grandmother asked him to stop at the old mill.

Its owner, Mr. Haydarov, began the late hours after noticing that students from the nearby college often walked past his dark windows on their way home from evening classes. stem.en:
Most of the apricots grown in the hills above Nodir's village are dried rather than sold fresh. On every farm the fruit ripens in the same two weeks of July, far more than the local markets can buy at once, and fresh apricots bruise easily on the long road to the city. Dried in the sun on flat rooftops, the fruit keeps for months and can be sold slowly through the winter, when prices are higher.

According to the text, why are most of the village's apricots dried?

options.en: Drying lets the farmers sell a large harvest slowly, not all at once.
Dried apricots sell for more in the city in July than fresh apricots do.
The farmers' rooftops are too small to store fresh fruit on.
Apricots in the hills ripen too late for the local markets.

stem.en:
For decades, the farmers of a mountain valley burned the dry stalks left in their fields after the harvest, believing the fire cleared the ground for the next crop. When a young farmer, Nodira, ploughed the stalks back into her soil instead, her neighbors expected a poor harvest. Her harvest was slightly smaller the first year, but in each of the next three years her field gave more grain than theirs, and by the fifth year half the valley had stopped burning its stalks.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

options.en: Nodira's method, doubted at first, proved better over time and spread.
Burning dry stalks clears the ground and improves the next crop.
Ploughing the stalks back into the soil gives a smaller harvest every year.
Young farmers are more willing than older ones to try new methods.

why.en: Her field gave less only the first year, then more grain each year, and half the valley copied her: the doubted method proved itself and spread.
why.uz: Uning dalasi faqat birinchi yili kamroq, keyin har yili koʻproq don berdi, vodiyning yarmi undan oʻrnak oldi: shubhali usul oʻzini oqladi.
why.ru: Её поле дало меньше лишь в первый год, потом каждый год больше, и полдолины переняли её способ: метод, в котором сомневались, оправдался.

A common complaint about the town's new bus timetable is that the buses now come less often: every fifteen minutes instead of every ten. The complaint is accurate, but it leaves out half of the change. The old buses often arrived in bunches, two or three together after a long gap, because they were stuck in the same traffic. The new route uses a lane kept for buses only, so they keep to the timetable, and the average wait at a stop is now shorter than before.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

options.en: Buses come less often now, but they keep to time, so passengers wait less.
The new buses come less often, so passengers now wait longer at every stop.
Buses arrive in bunches because of the town's traffic lights.
Every town should give its buses a lane of their own.

why.en: The text grants that buses come less often but adds the other half: a bus lane keeps them on time, so the average wait is now shorter.

He points out instead that a hand-cut spoon follows the grain of the wood, so it rarely splits, and that the families who buy his spoons often bring them back years later only to have the edges smoothed, not to replace them.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

Bahrom's hand-cut spoons are cheaper and more beautiful than machine-made ones.
A machine can make a hundred wooden spoons in a single hour.
Families prefer to replace their wooden spoons every few years.

why.en: He does not claim his spoons are cheaper or prettier; he says they follow the grain, rarely split and come back only to be smoothed: they last.

stem.en:
Planting trees along a busy road is usually described as a way to make a street greener. The residents of Shoira's neighborhood who planted plane trees along their main road had a more practical aim. The road had no shade, and in July the pavement grew so hot that older people stopped walking to the market at midday. Five summers later, the trees shade most of the pavement, and the market's busiest hour is once again noon.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

Trees are planted along roads mainly to make a street look greener.
The market in Shoira's neighborhood is busiest early in the morning.
Older people in the neighborhood prefer to do all of their shopping at midday.

When asked, most students at the school said that they prefer to read books that have bright, colorful covers.
The library bought more new books this year than it did last year.
Books shelved spine out take up less room than books displayed covers out.

Some of the seedlings were watered every day, and the others were watered twice a week.

The free class was so popular that the center added a second group.

After the town library began opening on Sunday afternoons, the number of books borrowed each week rose. The head librarian concluded that the Sunday hours had made people borrow more books.

Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken the head librarian's conclusion?

options.en: Hardly any books were borrowed on Sundays; the rise came on weekdays, after a large delivery of new books.
Many visitors told the librarians that they were glad they could now come to the library on Sunday afternoons.
Most of the library's Sunday visitors were families with young children.
On Sundays the library lent more books per hour than on any weekday.

why.en: If hardly any books went out on Sundays and the rise came on weekdays after new books arrived, the Sunday hours did not cause it. That weakens the conclusion.
why.uz: Agar yakshanba kunlari deyarli kitob olinmagan va oʻsish yangi kitoblar kelgach ish kunlarida boʻlgan boʻlsa, sabab yakshanba emas. Bu xulosani zaiflashtiradi.
why.ru: Если по воскресеньям книг почти не брали, а рост пришёлся на будни после поступления новых книг, дело не в воскресеньях. Это ослабляет вывод.

stem.en:
Ravshan noticed that the bread his family bakes at home rises higher on some days than on others. He thinks the dough rises higher when the kitchen is warmer.

Which finding, if true, would most directly support Ravshan's idea?

options.en: Dough from the same recipe rose highest on the warmest days and least on the coldest days.
Ravshan's family bakes bread three times a week, always in the morning.
Dough made from the same recipe rose to exactly the same height on warm days and on cold days.
Bread that rises higher is usually softer than bread that rises less.

why.en: His idea links warmth to rising. The finding that the same dough rose highest on the warmest days and least on the coldest supports it; another goes against it.
why.uz: Gʻoya issiqlikni xamirning koʻtarilishi bilan bogʻlaydi. Bir xil xamir eng issiq kunlarda eng baland, eng sovuq kunlarda eng past koʻtarilgani uni quvvatlaydi.

In a short story about a school football team, the narrator's friend Aziz is described as someone who hides his disappointment behind jokes, so that no one will feel sorry for him.

Komila hypothesized that looking after a plant makes people calmer. She gave a plant to half of her classmates for a month, and at the end, the classmates with plants said they felt calmer than the others did.

Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken Komila's hypothesis?

options.en: Classmates given a plant they never watered or touched felt just as calm as those who looked after theirs.
Classmates who were not given plants said that they felt less calm at the end of the month than they had at the start.
Classmates whose plants grew new leaves said they felt the calmest of all.
Most of Komila's classmates had never kept a plant of their own before.

why.en: If students who never cared for their plants felt as calm as those who did, looking after a plant is not what calms them. That weakens the hypothesis.
why.uz: Agar oʻsimligiga umuman qaramaganlar ham parvarish qilganlar kabi xotirjam boʻlsa, xotirjamlikni parvarish bermagan. Bu farazni zaiflashtiradi.
why.ru: Если те, кто вовсе не ухаживал за растением, были так же спокойны, как ухаживавшие, спокойствие даёт не уход. Это ослабляет гипотезу.

"Its stones are rounded smooth by a hundred years of carts, / and moss has filled the cracks along its sides."
"Each morning it carries the bread and the schoolchildren across, / as sure as the sun that climbs above the poplars."
"I stood on it once at dusk and dropped a stone, / and counted to three before I heard it fall."

why.en: Worn: stones 'rounded smooth by a hundred years of carts'. Dependable: 'still each morning it carries the bread across'. Only this quotation has both.

A coach noticed that the players on her team who drank more water during training made fewer passing mistakes. She concluded that drinking more water during training helps players pass more accurately.

Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken the coach's conclusion?

Players who drank more water during training also said that they felt less tired at the end of it.
The team trained outdoors in hot weather for most of the season.
Players who drank the least water made the most passing mistakes.

In a short story, a student claims that over the course of a year, the narrator's feelings about her new city change from loneliness to a sense of belonging.

Which quotation from the story most effectively illustrates the student's claim?

options.en: "In September I ate my lunch alone on the steps; by summer, the woman at the bakery was saving me the last warm loaf."
"In September I ate my lunch alone on the steps by the gate and counted the days until I could go home for the holidays."
"The city was louder than any place I had known, and its buses were always full."
"By summer, my friends from home were writing to me less and less often."

why.en: The claim is a change from loneliness to belonging. Eating alone in September and being saved a warm loaf by summer show both ends; the others show one moment.

most of the sparrows came to the fat-ball feeder, 4 of the 18.
more sparrows than tits came to the seed feeder, 14 against 3.
most of the tits came to the seed feeder, 3 of the 14.

A line graph shows the heights of two bean plants, A and B, measured four times, a week apart. Plant A: 4 cm, 9 cm, 15 cm and 22 cm. Plant B: 4 cm, 7 cm, 9 cm and 10 cm.

A student claims that plant A grew more than plant B in every one of the three weeks.

Which choice most effectively uses data from the graph to support the student's claim?

At the fourth measurement, plant A was 22 cm tall and plant B was 10 cm tall.
Plant A grew 2, 3 and 4 cm in the three weeks, while plant B grew 3, 2 and 1 cm.
Both plants were 4 cm tall when the first measurement was made.

why.en: 'Every one of the three weeks' needs each week's growth: A grew 5, 6 and 7 cm while B grew 3, 2 and 1 cm. The final heights alone do not show every week.
